page: Hetzner Cloud cax11 is an arm64-based virtual server belonging to the cax family, running on the QEMU hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs allocated from an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, with 2 physical cores and 1 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 1.95 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 40 GB NVMe SSD, and the server does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate entry-level performance characteristics. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is average at 1821.28, but multi-core scaling is weak at 3610.67. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with read-only large block speeds at 25.88 GB/sec and write speeds at 15.72 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database operations are also on the lower end, with a Passmark database score of 1355.63 and Redis SET operations reaching 2.58 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is recorded at 2.46 GB/sec.

Given its shared-core architecture and entry-level hardware specifications, the cax11 offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for lightweight workloads. It is best suited for low-traffic web serving, basic development environments, lightweight background tasks, and simple testing scenarios where high-performance multi-core execution or massive memory bandwidth is not required.

The platform provides a balanced entry point for ARM-based application testing.
